pages.name: Still there?
pages.task: You press Start on a DOL starter and let go. What keeps the contactor in?
pages.answer: A contact of the contactor itself, across Start
pages.why: Pulling in closes the contactor's own latching contact. It is wired across Start, so it keeps the coil fed after Start springs back.

pages.name: Coils and contacts apart
pages.text: A control schematic draws a circuit as numbered [[current paths]], from the supply at the top to the return at the bottom. Each coil sits in one path. Its contacts sit wherever they do their work. Each one carries the coil's tag. Coil -Q1 in path 2 is picked out together with its three contacts, in paths 3, 4 and 6.

pages.name: Find the coil
pages.task: The contact marked in path 2 is tagged -Q2. In which path is the coil that moves it?
pages.why: A contact belongs to the coil whose tag it carries. Coil -Q2 sits in path 4, so the contact in path 2 opens whenever -Q2 pulls in.

pages.name: The cross-reference
pages.text: Under each coil on this sheet sits its [[cross-reference]]. It lists the paths where that coil's contacts sit. Normally open ones are on the left, and normally closed ones on the right. Tapping -K1's contact in path 8 lights coil -K1 in path 1. Its table reads 2, 4 and then 8, and marks path 8.

pages.text: Contacts one after another in a path are in series. Any one opening drops the coil out, unless another path bridges it. The latching contact in path 3 is in parallel with Start 1. pages.text: A US ladder draws the same circuit sideways, as rungs between two rails. Each coil is a circle, here CR1, M1 and M2. Each contact carries its coil's tag. The same circuit is drawn as eight rungs. Coils CR1, M1 and M2 are circles at the right, and each contact is tagged with its coil.

pages.name: The circle on rung 2
pages.task: On the US ladder, what is the circle tagged M1 at the end of rung 2?
pages.why: In the US form, a coil is drawn as a circle. M1 is the coil of -Q1, the starter for the duty pump. Its contacts on rungs 3, 4 and 6 carry the tag M1. On the IEC sheet, -M1 is the motor itself.
